items.title: President launches book documenting govt's first 3 years
items.summary: The book, titled 156 Weeks in Service of the Nation and the People, is available for the public to read and download in digital format.

items.title: Respect campaign as important as infrastructure: President
items.summary: The President said the Maldives had reached a point where people showed little respect towards one another, despite being a Muslim nation.

items.title: Pres says delivered results across all sectors in 3 years
items.summary: The President maintained that the administration had not neglected any sector during the period.

items.title: High Court concludes hearing on Shahid's remand appeal
items.summary: Shahid, who has held several senior government positions, was arrested on the night of 2 November at his apartment in Rainbow Ocean Front, Hulhumalé.

items.title: JSC recommends Sameer for Supreme Court appointment
items.summary: Two candidates applied for the vacancy: former High Court judge Ali Sameer and serving High Court judge Abdul Rauf Ibrahim.

items.title: Govt will meet essential funding needs of institutions: Zareer
items.summary: Zareer said the government had considered the operational requirements of independent institutions when determining their budget allocations.

items.title: Corrections plans prison hospital to address delays in treatment
items.summary: He said the project remained in the documentation and planning stage and did not provide further details about the proposed facility.

items.title: Prison population rises 54% in 3 years, straining prison staff
items.summary: The current staffing ratio is approximately 4.6 inmates per officer, compared with the prescribed ratio of 1.75 inmates per officer.

items.title: Construction of Malé surfing stadium advancing, says president
items.summary: President Muizzu described the stadium as an important addition to the country's sports infrastructure.

items.title: Pension Office sacks COO Shiuna over code of conduct violation
items.summary: An official from the Pension Office confirmed that the decision followed an investigation into allegations of misconduct.
